text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in the Swedish papers this morning. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- More Swedes believe that the economy is improving. More households were positive about the country's economy over the next year according to a survey by Statistics Sweden in May and a purchasing managers' index showed the most positive outlook for two years.
- Two new companies are to be listed on the Stockholm bourse information list - InKina with operations in China and computer hardware company IFS.
- The investigation into the sinking of the Estonia ferry is to get a new head, Ann-Louise Eksborg, who will take over the Swedish part of the three-nation commission.

- Sweden's international credit rating of AA+ could still be raised as early as next year even if the government says no to EMU entry in 1999 when it releases its decision on EMU membership on Tuesday, according to Konrad Reuss, Standard & Poor's head for European ratings.
- Lock maker Assa Abloy's subsidiary VingCard is buying the Norwegian company Elsafe for 107 million Norwegian crowns, continuing its pace of acquisitions.

- A new stock exchange list called Hansalista is being launched in Skane, the southernmost region of Sweden. The new list is being developed by Kristianstad-based asset management company Spectra Kapitalforvaltning. The first company to be placed on the list will be the new Malmo Grip brewery.

- Swedish businessman Johan Eliasch is hoping to list Austrian sports company Head Tyrolia in New York. He took over the company in 1995 when it was under threat from competitors and last year it showed an operating profit for the first time sinced 1993. Today the U.S. accounts for 10 percent of the company's sales.

- AB Volvo picked up speed on the Swedish auto market last month while sales slipped for Saab, according to the Swedish Auto Manufacturers Association. Volvo's new car registrations in Sweden grew by 14 percent in May compared to the same month a year ago while Saab suffered a 15 percent drop.
